protocol.framing: 4-byte big-endian length followed by UTF-8 JSON
protocol.response: {"id": any, "ok": value} or {"id": any, "err": {"type": str, "msg": str}}

types.name: Gob
types.doc: A game object in the world (tree, animal, container, player...). A snapshot; call gobs.get to refresh.

fields.name: gob
fields.doc: Handle: the object's id. Pass the whole snapshot or this id to ops taking a Gob.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Resource name, e.g. "gfx/terobjs/trees/oak". Null while loading.

fields.name: hash
fields.doc: Stable identity that survives reloads (position + resource).

fields.name: rc
fields.doc: World position.

fields.name: a
fields.doc: Facing angle in radians.

fields.name: pose
fields.doc: Current pose resource, e.g. "gfx/borka/idle" (the first of `poses`).

fields.name: poses
fields.doc: All pose resources playing at once (composite objects can have several).

fields.name: attr
fields.doc: Model attribute: growth stage for crops and trees, fill flags for containers; -1 if none.

fields.name: overlays
fields.doc: Resource names of overlays (fire, contents, markers...).

fields.name: dist
fields.doc: Distance from the player when the snapshot was taken.

types.name: Item
types.doc: An inventory item. A snapshot; its handle stays valid while the item widget exists.

fields.name: item
fields.doc: Handle: the item widget id.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Display name, e.g. "Block of Birch".

fields.name: res
fields.doc: Resource name, e.g. "gfx/invobjs/wblock-birch".

fields.name: q
fields.doc: Quality.

fields.name: num
fields.doc: Number shown on the item (stack amount, uses), -1 if none.

fields.name: contents
fields.doc: Contents of containers (bucket, waterskin): [{name, q}].

fields.name: stack
fields.doc: Number of items in this item stack, 0 if it is not a stack.

fields.name: slot
fields.doc: Inventory cell [x, y] of the item's top-left corner.

fields.name: size
fields.doc: Size in inventory cells [w, h].

fields.name: parent
fields.doc: Widget id of the inventory or stack holding it.

types.name: Inventory
types.doc: An open inventory (the player's, or a container's).

fields.name: wdg
fields.doc: Handle: the inventory widget id.

fields.name: window
fields.doc: Caption of the window holding it.

fields.name: size
fields.doc: Size in cells [w, h].

types.name: Widget
types.doc: Any UI element. Windows add a caption.

fields.name: wdg
fields.doc: Handle: the widget id (server-assigned; -1 for client-only widgets).

fields.name: class
fields.doc: Java class name.

fields.name: caption
fields.doc: Window caption (windows only).

fields.name: parent
fields.doc: Parent widget id.

fields.name: visible
fields.doc: Whether it is shown.

fields.name: c
fields.doc: Position inside the parent, in UI pixels.

fields.name: sz
fields.doc: Size in UI pixels.

types.name: Area
types.doc: A saved area (zone) with its specialisations.

fields.name: area
fields.doc: Handle: the area id.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Area name.

fields.name: specs
fields.doc: Specialisations: [{name, subtype?}].

fields.name: rect
fields.doc: World rectangle; null if the area's part of the map is not loaded.

fields.name: in
fields.doc: Items configured to be taken from here.

fields.name: out
fields.doc: Items configured to be put here.

types.name: Coord
types.doc: A world position [x, y] in world units (11 units per tile).

types.name: Tile
types.doc: An integer pair [x, y]: a tile, an inventory cell, or a size.

types.name: Alias
types.doc: A name matcher: "text", ["a", "b"], or {"include": [...], "exclude": [...]}. Matches substrings of resource and display names, like the client's NAlias.

ops.name: core.describe
ops.doc: The API schema: every op with its parameters, types and docs. With `op`, only that op.

ops.name: core.ping
ops.doc: Round-trip check. Returns the client's time in milliseconds.

ops.name: core.version
ops.doc: API version and client build.

ops.returnsDoc: Subscription id, carried by each event as `sub`.
ops.name: events.subscribe
ops.doc: Starts delivering events of the given kinds from this run's session. `kind.*` subscribes to a whole family. Kinds: `ui.new`, `ui.add`, `ui.msg`, `ui.destroy`, `ui.out` (raw widget traffic), `combat.used`, `chat.msg`, `gob.new`, `gob.gone`, `form.*`. The filter keeps events whose data fields equal the given values; a string ending in `*` matches a prefix. Events are delivered asynchronously; use the SDK's `nc.events(...)` iterator or `nc.on(kind, fn)`.
ops.example:
for ev in nc.events("ui.new", caption="Cupboard*"):
    print(ev.data)

ops.name: events.unsubscribe
ops.doc: Stops a subscription.

ops.name: run.finish
ops.doc: Reports the script's outcome before it exits. A scenario step that runs this script continues only on success. Without this call, exit code 0 counts as success.

params.name: success
params.doc: True if the script did its job.

ops.name: run.params
ops.doc: Parameter values this run was started with: the answers to the script's header form, or a scenario step's settings.

ops.name: runs.close
ops.doc: Ends a run opened with runs.open after its queued requests finish. Closing the primary run ends the script's connection.

ops.name: runs.list
ops.doc: This connection's runs: the primary one and any opened with runs.open.

ops.name: runs.open
ops.doc: Starts a second bot thread bound to another session, for scripts that drive several characters. Requests carrying its run id execute on that session. The SDK wraps this as `nc.session(name)`, which returns a client for that character. The new run shows as its own row in that session's Bot Status strip and can be stopped on its own.

params.name: session
params.doc: Character name, username or session id.

ops.name: sessions.list
ops.doc: All logged-in sessions (tabs), visible and background.

ops.name: bots.get
ops.doc: One bot's description.

ops.returnsDoc: [{id, title, description, type, group, menu, scenario_step, interactive, class, params}]
ops.name: bots.list
ops.doc: Every bot registered in the client, including scripts in the Scripts folder, with their parameters.
ops.example:
for b in nc.bots.list():
    print(b["id"], b["title"])

ops.returnsDoc: True if the bot reported success.
ops.name: bots.run
ops.doc: Runs a registered bot on this script's bot thread and waits for it to finish. The bot behaves exactly as when started from the menu: it uses your areas and specialisations, shows its own dialogs, and stops with the script's stop button. A fresh instance is created for every run. Parameters are checked against the bot's declared settings.

ops.name: scenarios.list
ops.doc: Saved scenarios (bot chains) with their steps.

ops.name: scenarios.run
ops.doc: Runs a saved scenario step by step on this script's bot thread; stops at the first step that fails.

ops.name: player.attributes
ops.doc: Base attributes and skills from the character sheet. `base` holds strength, agility, intelligence, constitution, perception, charisma, dexterity, will and psyche under their short names (str, agi, int, con, prc, csm, dex, wil, psy); `skills` holds unarmed, melee, ranged, explore, stealth, sewing, smithing, masonry, carpentry, cooking, farming, survive, lore. Each entry is {base, comp}: `base` the trained value, `comp` the value after equipment and buffs. The values arrive with the character sheet at login; before that the dicts are empty.

ops.name: player.buffs
ops.doc: The buffs and debuffs shown in the buff bar: `res` (resource name), `name` (its tooltip name, null if none), and `meter` (the buff's progress meter in percent, -1 when it has none).
ops.example:
if any("drunk" in b["res"] for b in nc.player.buffs()):
    nc.chat.notify("sober up first")

ops.name: player.get
ops.doc: The character's current state in one call: the player's gob snapshot fields plus `character` (name), `stamina` and `energy` (fractions 0..1, null if the meter is not shown), `hp` {current, max, fraction, soft_fraction}, `speed` {cur, max} (0 crawl .. 3 sprint), `pose`, `moving`, `cursor` (cursor resource name, e.g. "gfx/hud/curs/arw") and `hand` (the item held on the cursor, or null). `hp.current`/`hp.max` come from the meter's tooltip and only update when it is hovered; use `hp.fraction` for safety checks.

ops.name: player.meters
ops.doc: Every meter on the HUD by its resource base name ("hp", "stam", "nrj", and others the server shows, such as the happiness/insanity meters). Each value is the list of bar fractions (0..1) in the meter, e.g. hp is [hard, soft] while wounded. Meters whose resource has not loaded are left out.

ops.name: player.set_speed
ops.doc: Sets the movement speed: 0 crawl, 1 walk, 2 run, 3 sprint. Values above the allowed maximum are clamped by the server.

ops.returnsDoc: Gob snapshots, nearest first unless sort="none".
ops.name: gobs.find
ops.doc: Finds game objects in the loaded part of the world. Filters combine (all must hold). Only objects whose resource has loaded are matched by `name`; the player's own object is never included (use `gobs.player`). To react to objects appearing or vanishing, subscribe to the `gob.new` event ({gob, name, rc}, sent once the object's resource is known; call `gobs.get` for the full snapshot) and `gob.gone` ({gob, name}). Without `radius` and `area` every loaded object is considered. `name` matches the resource name by substring ("trees/", "gfx/terobjs/chest"). Raises NotFound if `area` is given but is not loaded around the player (more than ~1000 units away or hidden): walk there first, an unloaded area would otherwise look empty.

params.name: area
params.doc: Only objects inside this area's rectangle.

params.name: radius
params.doc: Only objects closer than this to `near` (world units; a tile is 11).

params.name: near
params.doc: Centre for `radius` and for sorting; defaults to the player position.

params.name: pose
params.doc: Pose resource pattern(s), e.g. "knocked" or "dead"; objects without a pose never match.

params.name: attr
params.doc: Model attribute (crop stage, container fill marker, ...) must equal this. Note markers >= 128 read negative.

params.name: exclude
params.doc: Gob ids to skip (e.g. ones already processed).

params.name: limit
params.doc: At most this many results (after sorting); 0 = no limit.

ops.returnsDoc: Snapshot: gob, name, hash, rc, a, pose, attr, overlays, dist.
ops.name: gobs.get
ops.doc: A fresh snapshot of one game object, or null if it no longer exists in this session (out of view, destroyed, picked up). Never raises GobGone; use it to test whether a handle is still valid.

ops.returnsDoc: {begin: [x, y], end: [x, y], a, corners: [[x, y] x4], parts: [[[x, y] x4], ...]}
ops.name: gobs.hitbox
ops.doc: The object's collision box as the client's pathfinder sees it, or null if it has none (or its resource has not loaded). `begin`/`end` are the box corners in the object's own frame; `corners` are the four world-space corners after rotation; `parts` lists one corner set per part for objects with several solid parts (gates, passages).
ops.example:
hb = nc.gobs.hitbox(chest)
print(hb["corners"] if hb else "no hitbox")

ops.name: gobs.lifted
ops.doc: The object the player is carrying overhead (a lifted log, barrel, chest...), or null.

ops.name: gobs.nearest
ops.doc: The nearest game object matching the same filters as `gobs.find`, or null. Filters combine (all must hold). Only objects whose resource has loaded are matched by `name`; the player's own object is never included (use `gobs.player`). To react to objects appearing or vanishing, subscribe to the `gob.new` event ({gob, name, rc}, sent once the object's resource is known; call `gobs.get` for the full snapshot) and `gob.gone` ({gob, name}).

params.name: radius
params.doc: Only objects closer than this to `near`.

params.name: near
params.doc: Point to measure from; defaults to the player position.

ops.name: gobs.player
ops.doc: The player's own game object. For character state (stamina, hand, speed) use `player.get`.

ops.name: inv.count
ops.doc: How many items match `name`, counting each stack member as one item. This counts items, not amounts: a pile of seeds that is one item counts 1; sum `num` from `inv.items` for amounts.

params.name: inventory
params.doc: Inventory: "main" (default), a window caption such as "Cupboard", or an Inventory handle.

ops.name: inv.find
ops.doc: The first item whose display name matches `name` (stack members included), or null.

params.name: inventory
params.doc: Inventory: "main" (default), a window caption such as "Cupboard", or an Inventory handle.

ops.name: inv.free_slots
ops.doc: How many items of the given size still fit, placed without overlapping (the client's own space check, as Java bots use it). A 1x1 item is [1, 1]; a cheese tray is [1, 2]. Use the `size` field of an item snapshot.

params.name: inventory
params.doc: Inventory: "main" (default), a window caption such as "Cupboard", or an Inventory handle.

ops.name: inv.free_space
ops.doc: Number of empty cells in an inventory.

params.name: inventory
params.doc: Inventory: "main" (default), a window caption such as "Cupboard", or an Inventory handle.

ops.name: inv.hand
ops.doc: The item held on the cursor, or null.

ops.name: inv.item
ops.doc: A fresh snapshot of one item, or null if its widget no longer exists (moved to another inventory, used up, container closed). Works for items in inventories, stacks, equipment and the hand. Never raises ItemGone.

ops.name: inv.items
ops.doc: Items in an inventory, optionally filtered. `name` matches the item's display name ("Oak Block", "Cheese Tray"), case-insensitively by substring; resource paths such as "items/x" do not match. With `expand_stacks` (the default) the members of item stacks are listed one by one and the stack itself is not, which is what Java bots see; with `expand_stacks=False` you get the top-level grid items, stacks included as one item each (`stack` > 0). `quality_min` drops items below that quality (items without a quality are dropped too).

params.name: inventory
params.doc: Inventory: "main" (default), a window caption such as "Cupboard", or an Inventory handle.

params.name: quality_min
params.doc: Minimum quality (exact float, not the rounded display).

params.name: expand_stacks
params.doc: List stack members instead of stacks.

ops.name: inv.list
ops.doc: Every open inventory: the player's main inventory first, then those inside open windows (containers, belt, cupboards). Each snapshot carries `free`, the number of empty cells.
ops.example:
for inv in nc.inv.list():
    print(inv["window"], inv["free"])

ops.name: inv.stockpile
ops.doc: The open stockpile window's state, or null if none is open. `count` items are in the pile, `free` more fit, `capacity` = count + free; `res` is the piled item's resource name. Counts are null if the window has not shown them yet.

ops.name: equip.find
ops.doc: The first equipped item whose display name matches `name` (substring, case-insensitive), or null. Items still loading are skipped.
ops.example:
if nc.equip.find("Axe") is None:
    nc.chat.notify("equip an axe", error=True)

ops.name: equip.slots
ops.doc: Every equipment slot with the item in it, or null when empty. Slot names: head, accessory, shirt, armor_body, gloves, belt, hand_left, hand_right, ring_left, ring_right, robe, back, pants, armor_leg, cape, boots, store_hat, eyes, mouth, lfoot, rfoot, shoulder, coat. A two-handed tool appears in both hand slots.
ops.example:
eq = nc.equip.slots()
print(eq["hand_right"]["name"] if eq["hand_right"] else "empty hand")

ops.name: windows.buttons
ops.doc: The texts of the buttons in a window, in widget order. Click one with `ui.click_button(text, window=...)`. Icon-only buttons have no text and are left out.

ops.returnsDoc: True once the window is gone or hidden; false if it is still open after 5 s.
ops.name: windows.close
ops.doc: Closes a window the way its close button does, and waits up to 5 seconds for it to go away. Client-side windows such as the character sheet are hidden rather than destroyed; that counts as closed.

ops.name: windows.get
ops.doc: The newest window whose caption equals `caption` exactly, or null.

ops.name: windows.list
ops.doc: The open top-level windows (containers, crafting, character sheet, ...), newest last. Windows the client keeps hidden (the character sheet, equipment when closed) are left out unless `hidden` is true.

ops.name: windows.text
ops.doc: The texts shown in a window: every label and text field, in widget order. Rich-text boxes and drawn text are not included.

ops.name: areas.at
ops.doc: The visible areas containing a world position (areas can overlap). Only areas loaded around the player are considered.

params.name: pos
params.doc: World position, or a gob for its position.

ops.name: areas.by_spec
ops.doc: Enabled areas carrying a specialisation, optionally with a subtype (e.g. spec "crop", subtype "Carrot"). The names are those of `areas.specs`.
ops.example:
for field in nc.areas.by_spec("crop", subtype="Carrot"):
    print(field["name"])

ops.name: areas.containers
ops.doc: The storage containers inside an area that the client's bots know how to use (chests, crates, cupboards, sheds, baskets, tables, study desks, ...), nearest first. Each Gob snapshot has `cap`, the caption of the window it opens, which is what `inv.items(inventory=...)` accepts once it is open. Stockpiles and barrels are not included (use `gobs.find`). Raises NotFound if the area is not loaded around the player.
ops.example:
for box in nc.areas.containers("Cheese"):
    print(box["cap"], box["rc"])

ops.name: areas.for_item
ops.doc: Enabled areas configured to take in (`direction="in"`) or hand out (`"out"`) an item, by the item's exact display name, as set in the area's item lists. Loaded areas come first, nearest first; areas elsewhere in the world follow (their `rect` is null). For "out" areas each snapshot has `th`, the quality threshold of the matching entry (1 if none).

ops.name: areas.get
ops.doc: One area by id or name.

params.name: area
params.doc: Area id, exact name, or snapshot.

ops.returnsDoc: Area snapshots {area, name, specs, rect, in, out, disabled}, by id.
ops.name: areas.list
ops.doc: Every saved area of this world, enabled or not. `rect` is null for areas that are not loaded around the player; `disabled` areas are ignored by the client's bots.
ops.example:
for a in nc.areas.list():
    print(a["area"], a["name"], [s["name"] for s in a["specs"]])

ops.name: areas.specs
ops.doc: All specialisation names the client knows (the values `areas.by_spec` accepts).

ops.name: map.from_global
ops.doc: Converts a global position (grid id + offset, from `map.to_global`) back into this session's world coordinates, or null if that grid is not loaded here.

params.name: x
params.doc: Offset inside the grid, world units.

params.name: y
params.doc: Offset inside the grid, world units.

ops.name: map.path_length
ops.doc: How far the player would walk to reach a gob or position along the pathfinder's route, in world units (0 when already there), or null when there is no route. Never shorter than the straight-line distance.

params.name: target
params.doc: A gob (handle or id) or a world position [x, y].

ops.example:
trees = nc.gobs.find(name="trees/", radius=300)
best = min(trees, key=lambda t: nc.map.path_length(t) or 1e9)

ops.name: map.reachable
ops.doc: Whether the client's pathfinder finds a walkable route from the player to a game object (to a spot next to it) or to a position. Runs the pathfinder once without moving; it only knows the loaded area around the player, so far targets read as unreachable.

params.name: target
params.doc: A gob (handle or id) or a world position [x, y].

ops.name: map.tile
ops.doc: The terrain under a world position as its tile resource name, e.g. "gfx/tiles/grass", "gfx/tiles/water", "gfx/tiles/rocks/...". Null if that part of the map is not loaded.

params.name: pos
params.doc: World position, or a gob for its position.

ops.name: map.tiles
ops.doc: The tiles covering a world rectangle, optionally only those whose resource name matches `name`. At most 10000 tiles (100x100) per call; split larger rectangles. Tiles in unloaded grids are left out. `tile` is the tile coordinate (world position / 11, floored) and `rc` its centre in world units.
ops.example:
me = nc.gobs.player()["rc"]
water = nc.map.tiles([[me[0]-110, me[1]-110], [me[0]+110, me[1]+110]], name="water")

ops.name: map.to_global
ops.doc: Converts a world position of this session into a session-independent one: the map grid's id and the offset inside it (world units, 0..1100). World coordinates (`rc`) are only valid within one session and change after a relog; global ones can be stored and shared between characters. Null if the position's grid is not loaded.

params.name: pos
params.doc: World position, or a gob for its position.

ops.example:
spot = nc.map.to_global(nc.gobs.player())
# later, maybe in another session:
pos = nc.map.from_global(spot["grid"], spot["x"], spot["y"])

ops.name: chat.channels
ops.doc: The names of the open chat channels: "Area Chat", "Village", "Party", private chats by the other player's name, and log channels such as "System".

ops.name: chat.history
ops.doc: The most recent lines of a channel that the client still holds (everything since the channel opened in this session), oldest first. `from` is the sender's name where the client knows it (kin list names; null for system lines and unknown senders), `time` is the client's clock in seconds when the line arrived. For new lines as they arrive, subscribe to the `chat.msg` event ({channel, from, sender, text}).

params.name: limit
params.doc: At most this many lines (the newest).

ops.name: chat.notify
ops.doc: Shows a message in the game's message area, the line above the hotbar where "You found..." messages appear. With `error=True` it is shown in red with the error sound. Only this player sees it; nothing is sent to the server.

ops.name: chat.send
ops.doc: Sends a line to a chat channel, as if typed there. Other players see it. Log channels cannot be written to.

ops.name: actions.close
ops.doc: Closes a window (a container, a crafting window, any window) and waits until it is gone. Closing a window that is already gone does nothing.

params.name: window
params.doc: Window handle, an inventory inside it, or its caption.

params.name: timeout
params.doc: Seconds to wait for it to close.

ops.name: actions.collect_to_pile
ops.doc: Picks up matching items lying on the ground in one area and stockpiles them in another, emptying the inventory into piles whenever it fills. Runs until the source area is clear, no timeout.

params.name: source
params.doc: Area to pick items up from.

ops.name: actions.destroy
ops.doc: Destroys an object with the Destroy action (stumps, ruins, your own buildings) and waits until it is gone. Needs the right tool equipped (e.g. a shovel for stumps). Work stops when stamina runs out, so drink first for large objects. The cursor is reset afterwards, also on timeout.

params.name: timeout
params.doc: Seconds to wait for it to disappear.

ops.name: actions.dig
ops.doc: Starts digging at the character's feet (soil, clay, sand). Needs a shovel equipped. Returns once the digging pose starts; wait for it to end with wait.pose_not(player, "shoveldig").

params.name: timeout
params.doc: Seconds to wait for the digging pose.

ops.name: actions.drink
ops.doc: Drinks from your waterskins or other vessels until stamina reaches `level` (0..1). Does nothing if stamina is already there.

ops.name: actions.drop
ops.doc: Drops items on the ground at the character's feet and waits until they are gone from the inventory. Pass item handles, or an alias to drop every matching item of an inventory. Drops are paced to stay under the server's flood limit.

params.name: items
params.doc: Items, or an alias such as "Stone".

params.name: inventory
params.doc: Where to look up an alias; your own if omitted.

params.name: timeout
params.doc: Seconds to wait for the items to disappear.

ops.name: actions.drop_hand
ops.doc: Drops the item in hand on the ground at the character's feet and waits until the hand is empty. Does nothing if the hand is empty.

ops.name: actions.drop_hand_to_inventory
ops.doc: Puts the item in hand into the first free cell of an inventory and waits until the hand is empty. Does nothing if the hand is empty.

params.name: inventory
params.doc: Target inventory; your own if omitted.

ops.name: actions.eat
ops.doc: Eats the listed foods until energy reaches `energy` (0..1): first from your inventory, then from containers in the area with the "eat" specialisation, walking there if needed.

params.name: items
params.doc: Food names, in order of preference.

ops.name: actions.equip
ops.doc: Equips a tool or weapon in the hands, taking it from the belt or the inventory and putting away what was held if needed. Does nothing if it is already in a hand.

ops.name: actions.face
ops.doc: Turns the character to face a position or game object without walking there, and waits until it does.

params.name: timeout
params.doc: Seconds to wait for the turn.

ops.name: actions.fill_troughs
ops.doc: Feeds matching items from your inventory into troughs, moving on to the next trough when one is full. Runs until done, no timeout.

ops.name: actions.fill_waterskins
ops.doc: Refills your waterskins and other water containers at the nearest water area (the "water" specialisation). Runs until done, no timeout.

params.name: global
params.doc: Use global navigation to reach a far water area.

ops.name: actions.flower
ops.doc: Right-clicks a game object and chooses an option from its flower menu, then waits for the menu to close. Pass a list to try several options in order (e.g. ["Chop", "Chop into blocks"]); the first one the menu offers is chosen. The server walks the character to the object by itself, so no path_to is needed for reachable objects. This op returns once the option is chosen, not when the work is finished: follow it with a wait such as wait.pose_not.

params.name: option
params.doc: Option text, or candidates in order of preference. Exact match.

params.name: timeout
params.doc: Seconds to wait for the menu to appear.

ops.name: actions.flower_item
ops.doc: Right-clicks an inventory item and chooses an option from its flower menu (e.g. "Eat", "Split", "Drink"), then waits for the menu to close.

params.name: option
params.doc: Option text, or candidates in order of preference. Exact match.

params.name: timeout
params.doc: Seconds to wait for the menu to appear.

ops.name: actions.free_inventory
ops.doc: Puts everything in your inventory away into the areas set up for it (the item's "out" areas and specialisations), like the bots do at the end of a cycle. Items with no area stay in the inventory. Walks wherever needed; runs until done, no timeout.

ops.name: actions.go_to_area
ops.doc: Travels to an area using the client's navigation: the local pathfinder when the area is near, otherwise the global chunk navigation (roads, doors, stairs) the bots use. With `enter` (the default) it also walks onto the area so its objects are loaded; without it, an area that is already reachable is not walked to. Runs until the navigation finishes; there is no timeout.

params.name: enter
params.doc: Walk onto the area even if it is already reachable.

ops.name: actions.harvest
ops.doc: Harvests every ripe plant of a crop in a field area, like the farmer bots: products go to their out areas, seeds to the seed area's barrels or containers, leftovers to troughs. Runs until the field is done, no timeout.

params.name: seed
params.doc: Area holding the seed barrels / containers.

ops.name: actions.lift
ops.doc: Walks to an object and lifts it (carry), then waits until the character holds it.

params.name: timeout
params.doc: Seconds to wait for the lift after arriving.

ops.name: actions.light
ops.doc: Lights a fireplace, oven, kiln, smelter or other burnable workstation with whatever the client can use (a torch or candelabrum, or fire from branches), like the right-click "Light" menu. Runs until done, no timeout.

ops.returnsDoc: True if the tile changed (was mined out), false on timeout.
ops.name: actions.mine
ops.doc: Walks next to a rock tile (or a cave wall) and mines it, then waits until the tile changes. Needs a pickaxe equipped. Mining stops when stamina runs out; drink and call again. The cursor is reset afterwards.

params.name: pos
params.doc: World position anywhere on the tile.

params.name: timeout
params.doc: Seconds to wait for the tile to change.

ops.returnsDoc: The container's inventory, or its window if it has no item grid (stockpiles, barrels).
ops.name: actions.open
ops.doc: Walks to a container (chest, cupboard, cart, stockpile, barrel...) and opens it. If its window is already open it is reused. A container that answers with an "Open" flower menu (cauldrons, study desks) is opened through it. Close it again with actions.close when done.

params.name: timeout
params.doc: Seconds to wait for the window after arriving.

ops.name: actions.path_to
ops.doc: Walks to a game object or a world position with the client's pathfinder, avoiding obstacles. For a game object it stops next to it, close enough to interact. `hard` mode walks right up to the object's edge (what container and pile bots use). Only works within the loaded area around the player; use actions.go_to_area for long distances. Runs until the pathfinder arrives or gives up; there is no timeout.

params.name: target
params.doc: Game object, or a world position [x, y].

params.name: hard
params.doc: Walk right up to the object's hitbox instead of the nearest free spot.

ops.name: actions.place
ops.doc: Walks next to a spot and puts the carried object down there at the given angle, then waits until it is placed.

params.name: pos
params.doc: World position for the object's centre.

params.name: gob
params.doc: The carried object; found automatically if omitted.

params.name: timeout
params.doc: Seconds to wait for placement after arriving.

ops.name: actions.restore_resources
ops.doc: Restores stamina and energy the way the bots do: drinks below 50% stamina (refilling waterskins at a water area if needed), eats from the eating area below 35% energy, then walks back. Runs until done, no timeout.

ops.name: actions.seed
ops.doc: Plants a crop on every free tile of a field area, taking seeds from the seed area. Runs until the field is planted, no timeout.

params.name: seed
params.doc: Area holding the seed barrels / containers.

ops.name: actions.stop
ops.doc: Stops the character where it stands (a left click on its own position). Cancels walking and most ongoing work.

ops.returnsDoc: Number of items that arrived in your inventory.
ops.name: actions.take_from
ops.doc: Takes items from a container into your inventory. With a game object, walks to it, opens it, takes and closes it again; with an open inventory (or its window caption), takes directly. Takes as many as fit, up to `count`.

params.name: container
params.doc: Container object, or an open inventory / window caption.

params.name: count
params.doc: Maximum number of items; all matching if omitted.

params.name: quality_min
params.doc: Only items of at least this quality.

params.name: timeout
params.doc: Seconds to wait for the container window when opening a game object.

ops.name: actions.take_from_barrel
ops.doc: Walks to a barrel and takes its contents into your inventory, `count` items or as many as fit. Runs until done, no timeout.

params.name: count
params.doc: How many; as many as fit if omitted.

ops.name: actions.take_from_pile
ops.doc: Walks to a stockpile, opens it and takes up to `count` items into your inventory, then closes it. A pile that is emptied disappears from the world.

params.name: count
params.doc: Maximum number of items; as many as fit if omitted.

ops.returnsDoc: How many matching items are in your inventory afterwards.
ops.name: actions.take_items
ops.doc: Fetches items from the areas where they are stored (the item's "in" areas) into your inventory, walking there as needed. Counts include what you already carry. Runs until done, no timeout.

params.name: name
params.doc: Exact item name, e.g. "Block of Pine".

params.name: count
params.doc: How many you want to have.

ops.returnsDoc: The item now in the hand.
ops.name: actions.take_to_hand
ops.doc: Picks an item up onto the cursor (the hand) and waits until it is there. If something is already in the hand the two are swapped, as in the game.

ops.name: actions.to_piles
ops.doc: Puts matching items from your inventory into stockpiles inside an area, filling existing piles first and starting new ones where there is room. Walks onto the area first. Runs until done, no timeout. Use an area that only holds piles of this item.

ops.returnsDoc: Number of items that left your inventory.
ops.name: actions.transfer
ops.doc: Moves items from your inventory into a container. With a game object, walks to it, opens it, transfers and closes it again; with an open inventory (or its window caption), transfers directly. Moves as many as fit, up to `count`. Different item kinds matching the alias are moved one kind after another.

params.name: to
params.doc: Container object, or an open inventory / window caption.

params.name: items
params.doc: Which items to move (name match, as everywhere).

params.name: count
params.doc: Maximum number of items to move; all matching if omitted.

params.name: timeout
params.doc: Seconds to wait for the container window when opening a game object.

ops.name: actions.transfer_items
ops.doc: Delivers the named items from your inventory to their "out" areas, walking as needed. Unlike free_inventory, only the listed item names are moved. Runs until done, no timeout.

ops.name: actions.transfer_to_barrel
ops.doc: Walks to a barrel and pours matching items from your inventory into it (seeds, flour, water from buckets...). Runs until done, no timeout.

ops.name: actions.travel_to_hearth
ops.doc: Travels to your hearth fire (the "Travel home" action) and waits until you arrive.

ops.name: actions.use_on_gob
ops.doc: Uses the item in hand on a game object, like clicking the object while holding it (water into a trough, seeds into a pot, a log into a chipping block). If `item` is given it is first picked up into the hand. Does not wait for the result; follow it with a wait (wait.hand_free, wait.pose_not...).

params.name: item
params.doc: Item to pick up first; otherwise the item already in hand is used.

params.name: all
params.doc: Shift-click: repeat with every matching item (e.g. fill all seeds).

params.name: timeout
params.doc: Seconds to wait for the item to reach the hand.

ops.name: actions.use_on_item
ops.doc: Uses the item in hand on another item (pour a bucket into a jar, put a whetstone on a tool, combine). If `source` is given that item is picked up first. Does not wait for the result.

params.name: target
params.doc: Item to use the hand on.

params.name: source
params.doc: Item to pick up first; otherwise the item already in hand is used.

params.name: timeout
params.doc: Seconds to wait for the source to reach the hand.

ops.name: craft.close
ops.doc: Closes the crafting window if it is open.

ops.returnsDoc: [{name, res, act}] where `act` is the entry's action path, e.g. ["craft", "cheesetray"].
ops.name: craft.list
ops.doc: Crafting recipes your character knows (the menu grid's craft entries), with their display name and resource. `filter` keeps entries whose name or resource contains the text (case-insensitive). With `all`, every menu entry is listed (actions, buildings...), not only crafts. Entries whose resources are still loading are skipped.

params.name: filter
params.doc: Substring of the name or resource.

params.name: all
params.doc: List every menu entry, not only craft recipes.

ops.example:
for r in nc.craft.list(filter="tray"):
    print(r["name"], r["res"])

ops.returnsDoc: True if crafting started; false if nothing happened within 5 s (some recipes finish instantly without a progress bar).
ops.name: craft.make
ops.doc: Presses Craft (or Craft All) in the open crafting window. Waits up to 5 seconds for the work to start (the hourglass progress bar); a game error such as missing ingredients raises ActionFailed. With `wait` (the default) it then waits until the progress bar has been gone for 1.5 s, so a Craft All run is finished, not just its first item.

params.name: wait
params.doc: Wait for the crafting to finish.

params.name: timeout
params.doc: Seconds to wait for it to finish.

ops.returnsDoc: The window as craft.window describes it.
ops.name: craft.open
ops.doc: Opens the crafting window for a recipe, by its display name or resource name (see craft.list), and waits until the window shows that recipe with its ingredient names loaded.

params.name: name
params.doc: Recipe display name ("Cheese Tray") or resource ("paginae/craft/cheesetray").

params.name: timeout
params.doc: Seconds to wait for the window.

ops.name: craft.wait_done
ops.doc: Waits until the hourglass progress bar has been gone for `quiet` seconds: the current craft (or any timed action) is over. Returns at once if nothing is in progress and has not been for `quiet` seconds.

params.name: quiet
params.doc: Seconds without a progress bar that count as done.

ops.returnsDoc: {wdg, recipe, res, inputs: [{name, res, count, chosen}], outputs: [...], tools: [res], loaded}
ops.name: craft.window
ops.doc: Describes the open crafting window: the recipe, its inputs and outputs with counts, and the tools it needs. `chosen` is the ingredient picked for a generic input (e.g. which "Raw Meat"), if any. Returns null if no crafting window is open.
ops.example:
w = nc.craft.window()
if w: print(w["recipe"], [i["name"] for i in w["inputs"]])

ops.name: wait.cursor
ops.doc: Waits until the mouse cursor's resource name contains `name`, e.g. "mine", "dig", "arw" (normal).

ops.name: wait.energy
ops.doc: Waits until energy is at least `at_least` (0..1; 1 = 10000 energy points).

ops.name: wait.flower_menu
ops.doc: Waits until a flower (right-click) menu is open and returns its options. Choose one with raw.flower_choose.

ops.name: wait.flower_menu_closed
ops.doc: Waits until no flower menu is open. Returns at once if none is.

ops.name: wait.gob_appears
ops.doc: Waits until a game object whose resource name matches `name` exists within `radius` of the player, and returns the nearest one. Returns at once if one is already there.

params.name: radius
params.doc: Distance from the player in world units (a tile is 11).

ops.name: wait.gob_attr
ops.doc: Waits until a game object's model attribute (the `attr` field of its snapshot: fill level, stage, lit state...) equals `value`, or, without `value`, until it changes from what it is now.

params.name: value
params.doc: Wanted value; omit to wait for any change.

ops.name: wait.gob_gone
ops.doc: Waits until a game object no longer exists (destroyed, picked up, felled, or out of view). Returns at once if it is already gone.

ops.name: wait.hand_free
ops.doc: Waits until nothing is on the cursor (the hand is empty). Returns at once if it already is.

ops.name: wait.inventory_free
ops.doc: Waits until an inventory has at least `cells` free cells.

ops.name: wait.item_in_hand
ops.doc: Waits until an item is on the cursor (the hand), optionally one whose name matches.

params.name: name
params.doc: Name match; any item if omitted.

ops.name: wait.items
ops.doc: Waits until an inventory holds at least `count` items matching `name` (stacked items count one by one).

ops.name: wait.items_at_most
ops.doc: Waits until an inventory holds at most `count` items matching `name` (e.g. until they are used up or moved away).

ops.name: wait.near
ops.doc: Waits until the player is within `dist` of a position or game object (e.g. after a walk started with raw.click_ground).

ops.name: wait.not_moving
ops.doc: Waits until the player has stopped moving (no movement and no walking pose).

ops.name: wait.player_idle
ops.doc: Waits until the player is idle: not moving, no hourglass progress bar, and the pose is one of the idle poses (standing, or standing while carrying something).

ops.name: wait.plob_ready
ops.doc: Waits until a placement ghost (a building blueprint or a carried object being placed) is loaded and ready to place with raw.place.

ops.name: wait.pose
ops.doc: Waits until a game object's (usually the player's) animation pose contains one of the given texts, e.g. "chop", "shoveldig", "gfx/borka/idle".

ops.returnsDoc: The pose afterwards, or null if the object is gone.
ops.name: wait.pose_not
ops.doc: Waits until a game object's pose no longer contains any of the given texts: the work it shows has ended (chopping stopped because the tree fell, or stamina ran out). Also ends if the object disappears.

ops.name: wait.progress
ops.doc: Waits until the hourglass progress bar appears: a timed action (crafting, building, butchering) has started.

ops.name: wait.progress_done
ops.doc: Waits until no hourglass progress bar is shown: the timed action finished or was interrupted. Returns at once if none is shown. For Craft All, which shows a new bar per item, prefer craft.wait_done.

ops.name: wait.seconds
ops.doc: Sleeps for a number of seconds of wall-clock time. Unlike Python's time.sleep it ends at once when the script is stopped.

params.name: seconds
params.doc: How long; 0 or less returns at once.

ops.name: wait.stamina
ops.doc: Waits until stamina is at least `at_least` (0..1), e.g. while resting.

ops.name: wait.ticks
ops.doc: Waits for a number of client ticks (frames of the game logic, roughly the frame rate).

ops.name: wait.window
ops.doc: Waits until a window with the given caption is open. A caption ending in `*` matches a prefix ("Cupboard*").

params.name: caption
params.doc: Window caption, exact or with a trailing `*`.

ops.name: wait.window_closed
ops.doc: Waits until a window is gone. Pass a handle for one particular window, or a caption to wait until no window with it is open.

params.name: window
params.doc: Window handle, an inventory in it, or a caption.

ops.returnsDoc: The combat state after the attack (see combat.state).
ops.name: combat.attack
ops.doc: Attacks an object with the Aggro action (as clicking it with the attack cursor does), waits until it appears in the fight list, and puts the normal cursor back.

params.name: timeout
params.doc: Seconds to wait for the fight to start.

ops.returnsDoc: How many opponents were offered peace.
ops.name: combat.peace
ops.doc: Offers peace (the white flag on the portrait) to one opponent, or to every opponent that has not been offered it yet, and waits until the client shows the flag raised. Animals being tamed and players who accept leave the fight.

params.name: gob
params.doc: The opponent; omit for all of them.

params.name: timeout
params.doc: Seconds to wait for the flags.

ops.returnsDoc: {target, opponents: [{gob, name, pose, dist, current, ip, oip, give, last_action, last_action_age, openings, stance, buffs}], me: {openings, stance, buffs, last_action}, cooldown, cooldown_total, moves: [{slot, name, cooldown, ready}]}
ops.name: combat.state
ops.doc: The current fight as the client sees it, or null when not fighting. Openings are 0-100 per colour (`offbalance` green, `reeling` yellow, `cornered` red, `dizzy` blue). `opponents[].openings` are the openings you have made on that opponent; `me.openings` are theirs on you. `ip`/`oip` are your and their initiative points against that opponent; `give` is the peace-flag state (1 = you offered peace). `cooldown` is the seconds left before you can act again; `moves` is the action bar (slot 0 = key 1, slot 5 = Shift+1). Resource names may be null for a moment while they load.
ops.example:
st = nc.combat.state()
if st and st["cooldown"] == 0:
    tgt = next(o for o in st["opponents"] if o["current"])
    print(tgt["name"], tgt["openings"]["cornered"])

ops.returnsDoc: True once it is the current target, false if the server did not switch in time.
ops.name: combat.target
ops.doc: Makes another opponent in the fight list the current target (what Ctrl+Tab or clicking its portrait does) and waits until the server confirms.

params.name: gob
params.doc: An opponent in the fight list (an id works after it left view).

params.name: timeout
params.doc: Seconds to wait for the switch.

ops.example:
weakest = min(st["opponents"], key=lambda o: o["dist"] or 99)
nc.combat.target(weakest["gob"])

ops.name: combat.use
ops.doc: Uses a move from the combat action bar against the current target, like pressing its key. `move` is a slot number (0-9, see combat.state `moves`) or a move's resource name; a name matches exactly, by its last part ("barrage" for "paginae/atk/barrage"), or as a substring. With `wait` (the default) it first waits for your cooldown and the move's own cooldown to run out.

params.name: wait
params.doc: Wait until the move is ready before using it.

params.name: timeout
params.doc: Seconds to wait for the move to be ready.

params.name: pos
params.doc: World position for moves aimed at the ground (what the mouse would point at).

ops.returnsDoc: Values by field name (label fields are left out).
ops.name: form.ask
ops.doc: Shows a settings form in the client's own style and waits until the player presses OK. Each field is a dict `{name, type, label, default, values, required}`. Types: `int` and `float` (a number entry), `bool` (a check box), `str` (a text entry), `choice` (a dropdown of `values`), `area` (the saved areas, plus "Select on map..." which lets the player drag a rectangle after OK; set `"map": false` to allow saved areas only), `gob` (a button that lets the player click an object), and `label` (static text, no value; give the text as `label`). `label` defaults to `name`; `required` fields marked with * must be filled before OK is accepted. An `area` field returns the area id, or a Rect `[[x1, y1], [x2, y2]]` when the player chose "Select on map..."; a `gob` field returns the object id (null if none was picked and the field is optional). Empty optional number fields are null. Needs a visible session.

params.name: fields
params.doc: Field specs, shown top to bottom.

params.name: timeout
params.doc: Seconds to wait; 0 waits until the player answers.

ops.example:
cfg = nc.form.ask("Chopper", [
    {"name": "area", "type": "area", "label": "Trees", "required": True},
    {"name": "count", "type": "int", "label": "How many", "default": 10},
    {"name": "axe", "type": "choice", "values": ["Stone Axe", "Metal Axe"]},
    {"name": "stack", "type": "bool", "label": "Stack logs", "default": True},
])
print(cfg["count"], cfg["area"])

ops.name: form.confirm
ops.doc: Asks a yes/no question in a small window and waits for the answer. Closing the window counts as No. Needs a visible session.

params.name: title
params.doc: Window caption; defaults to the script's name.

params.name: timeout
params.doc: Seconds to wait; 0 waits until the player answers.

ops.name: form.message
ops.doc: Shows an information window with an OK button and returns at once. The window closes when the player presses OK, or when the run ends unless `keep` is true. Needs a visible session.

params.name: title
params.doc: Window caption; defaults to the script's name.

params.name: keep
params.doc: Leave the window open after the run ends (for a final report).

ops.returnsDoc: `[[x1, y1], [x2, y2]]`, top-left and bottom-right corners.
ops.name: form.pick_area
ops.doc: Asks the player to drag a rectangle on the map, exactly like a bot's "select area" step, and returns it in world coordinates. The rectangle snaps to whole tiles. A small window shows the prompt with a Cancel button. Needs a visible session.

params.name: timeout
params.doc: Seconds to wait; 0 waits until the player selects or cancels.

ops.example: (x1, y1), (x2, y2) = nc.form.pick_area("Select the field to plough")

ops.name: form.pick_gob
ops.doc: Asks the player to click an object on the map and returns it, the same way built-in bots ask for a container or a vehicle. A small window shows the prompt with a Cancel button. Needs a visible session.

params.name: timeout
params.doc: Seconds to wait; 0 waits until the player picks or cancels.

ops.example:
barrel = nc.form.pick_gob("Click the water barrel")
print(barrel.name)

ops.returnsDoc: The text as typed (may be empty).
ops.name: form.text
ops.doc: Asks the player to type a line of text and waits for OK. Needs a visible session.

params.name: prompt
params.doc: What to ask, shown above the entry.

params.name: title
params.doc: Window caption; defaults to the script's name.

params.name: timeout
params.doc: Seconds to wait; 0 waits until the player answers.

ops.example: name = nc.form.text("Name for the new area:", default="Logs")

ops.name: overlay.clear
ops.doc: Removes every overlay this run created. The client does this by itself when the run ends.

ops.name: overlay.ghost
ops.doc: Shows a translucent placement ghost of a resource's model at a position, like the build bots' previews. The resource is loaded and checked first; a name that does not exist or has nothing to draw is rejected.

params.name: pos
params.doc: World position [x, y], or a gob's position.

ops.name: overlay.highlight
ops.doc: Tints a game object, like the client's item-search highlight. Colour as "#rrggbb", "#rrggbbaa" or [r, g, b] / [r, g, b, a] (0-255). The colour's alpha is the strength of the tint (255 paints a flat silhouette). The highlight lasts while the object stays loaded; it is removed with overlay.remove, overlay.clear or when the run ends.

ops.name: overlay.label
ops.doc: Shows outlined text above a game object or at a world position. Colour as "#rrggbb", "#rrggbbaa" or [r, g, b] / [r, g, b, a] (0-255).

params.name: at
params.doc: An object (the label follows it) or a world position [x, y].

params.name: height
params.doc: Height above the ground, in world units.

ops.name: overlay.line
ops.doc: Draws a line through world points on the ground (a route, a fence plan). It is drawn on top of everything and follows the terrain. Colour as "#rrggbb", "#rrggbbaa" or [r, g, b] / [r, g, b, a] (0-255).

params.name: points
params.doc: World positions [[x, y], ...] (gob snapshots work too); at least two.

params.name: closed
params.doc: Join the last point back to the first.

ops.name: overlay.marker
ops.doc: Puts a temporary marker with a label on the minimap and the map window (it is not saved as a map marker). Colour as "#rrggbb", "#rrggbbaa" or [r, g, b] / [r, g, b, a] (0-255).

params.name: pos
params.doc: World position [x, y], or a gob's position.

ops.name: overlay.rect
ops.doc: Draws a rectangle on the ground like a saved area: a translucent fill over the tiles it covers and a border at its exact edges, with an optional label in the middle. Colour as "#rrggbb", "#rrggbbaa" or [r, g, b] / [r, g, b, a] (0-255). The fill uses the colour at about a third of its alpha.

params.name: rect
params.doc: World rectangle [[x1, y1], [x2, y2]], e.g. from form.pick_area or an area snapshot.

ops.returnsDoc: False if there was no such overlay (already removed).
ops.name: overlay.remove
ops.doc: Removes one overlay this run created.

params.name: id
params.doc: Overlay id returned by an overlay.* call.

ops.name: overlay.tiles
ops.doc: Fills a set of map tiles with a translucent colour, e.g. to show planned plots or the tiles a bot will dig. Colour as "#rrggbb", "#rrggbbaa" or [r, g, b] / [r, g, b, a] (0-255). At most 20000 tiles per overlay.

params.name: color
params.doc: Fill colour; its alpha is the opacity.

ops.example:
tc = [[x, y] for x in range(10, 20) for y in range(5, 8)]
nc.overlay.tiles(tc, color=[64, 192, 255, 80])

ops.name: raw.click_gob
ops.doc: Clicks a game object like the mouse would. Button 1 is left, 3 is right (opens the flower menu). `mods`: 1 shift, 2 ctrl, 4 alt (add them). Does not walk there first and does not wait.

params.name: meshid
params.doc: Model part to click (doors, sub-meshes); -1 for the whole object.

params.name: offset
params.doc: Click point relative to the object's centre, in its own rotation.

ops.name: raw.click_ground
ops.doc: Clicks the ground at a world position. A left click walks there (without pathfinding); with a menu action armed (raw.menu_act) it applies the action there.

ops.name: raw.cursor
ops.doc: Name of the current mouse cursor resource, e.g. "arw" (normal), "dig", "mine", "chi" (carry).

ops.returnsDoc: False if the menu has no such option (the menu is then closed).
ops.name: raw.flower_choose
ops.doc: Chooses an option of the open flower menu by its exact text. Pass null to close the menu without choosing.

ops.name: raw.flower_options
ops.doc: Options of the open flower (right-click) menu, or an empty list if none is open.

ops.name: raw.inv_drop
ops.doc: Drops the item in hand into an inventory cell.

params.name: inventory
params.doc: Target inventory ("main", a window caption, or a handle).

ops.name: raw.invxf
ops.doc: Moves items from one open inventory to another the way shift+mouse-wheel does: `count` items, taken by the server in its own order. Use actions.transfer for name-based moves.

ops.name: raw.item_drop
ops.doc: Drops an item on the ground at the player's feet (ctrl-click).

ops.name: raw.item_interact
ops.doc: Right-clicks an item: opens its flower menu (Eat, Split, Drink...). Choose with raw.flower_choose or actions.flower_item.

ops.name: raw.item_take
ops.doc: Picks an item up onto the cursor (the hand). Does not wait; see wait.item_in_hand.

ops.name: raw.item_transfer
ops.doc: Shift-clicks an item: moves it to the other open inventory (or out of a container into yours).

ops.name: raw.itemact_gob
ops.doc: Uses the item in hand on a game object (like clicking it while holding the item).

ops.name: raw.itemact_ground
ops.doc: Uses the item in hand on the ground at a position.

ops.name: raw.itemact_item
ops.doc: Uses the item in hand on another item (e.g. pour water into a bucket, combine).

ops.name: raw.menu_act
ops.doc: Triggers a menu-grid action by its internal name, as if its button or hotkey were used: e.g. ["carry"], ["destroy"], ["mine"], ["dig"], ["aggro"], ["croster"], ["bp", "palisade"]. Most arm the cursor; follow with raw.click_gob or raw.click_ground.

ops.name: raw.pagina_use
ops.doc: Uses a menu-grid entry (pagina) by its display name or resource name, e.g. "Drink" or "paginae/act/drink". Crafting recipes open their craft window this way.

ops.name: raw.place
ops.doc: Places the object being placed (a carried object or a build ghost) at a position and angle. Arm it first (e.g. raw.click_gob with shift on a carried object, or a build recipe).

ops.name: ui.click_button
ops.doc: Clicks the first button whose text equals `text` (inside `window` if given).

ops.name: ui.find
ops.doc: Searches the widget tree for widgets whose Java class name ends with `cls` and/or whose caption or text contains `text`.

params.name: text
params.doc: Substring of a window caption, button or label text.

ops.name: ui.tree
ops.doc: The widget tree below a widget (default: the game UI). Each node is a Widget snapshot plus `children`, and `text` for buttons and labels. Use `depth` to keep it small; the full tree has thousands of nodes.

params.name: depth
params.doc: Levels below the root; -1 for all.

ops.example:
tree = nc.ui.tree(depth=1)
print([c["class"] for c in tree["children"]])

ops.name: ui.wdgmsg
ops.doc: Sends a raw widget message to the server, exactly as the widget would. Coordinates in `args` are passed as [x, y] lists and converted to Coord; use `raw.*` ops for world positions, which need server units.

ops.name: ui.widget
ops.doc: One widget's snapshot, or null if it no longer exists.

ops.name: java.call
ops.doc: Calls a method on an object, or reads a field when there is no such method and no arguments. The target is a reference, a snapshot (Gob, Item, Widget, Area), or one of "gui", "ui", "map", "player", "glob", "inventory", "run".

ops.name: java.get
ops.doc: Reads a field (any visibility) of an object, or a static field when `target` is a class name prefixed with "class:".

ops.name: java.items
ops.doc: Converts a referenced Collection, Map (its entries as [key, value]), Iterable or array to a list, element by element.

ops.name: java.members
ops.doc: Lists the methods and fields of a class or of a referenced object's class, for exploring the client from a REPL.

params.name: filter
params.doc: Only members whose name contains this.

ops.name: java.new
ops.doc: Constructs an object and returns a reference to it.

ops.name: java.ref
ops.doc: Turns a snapshot or special name into a reference, e.g. to call several methods on the same object.

ops.name: java.release
ops.doc: Releases references so the objects can be garbage collected. All references are released when the script disconnects.

ops.returnsDoc: True if the action returned SUCCESS.
ops.name: java.run_action
ops.doc: Constructs any nurgling.actions.Action by class name and runs it on this script's bot thread, as Java bots do: `new X(args...).run(gui)`. Gives scripts every reusable action in the client, including ones the curated API does not wrap.

ops.name: java.set
ops.doc: Writes a field (any visibility, not final) of an object, or a static field with "class:Name".

ops.name: java.static
ops.doc: Calls a static method, or reads a static field when there is no method of that name and no arguments.

errors.BadArgs: Missing, unknown or wrongly typed arguments.
errors.ActionFailed: A game action ran but reported failure (the Java action returned FAIL or ERROR).
errors.Stopped: The run was stopped (stop button, script exit, or session closed). Not catchable as a normal failure: the run is over.
errors.Timeout: A wait or blocking call did not finish within its timeout.
errors.JavaError: A Java exception thrown inside a java.* call (layer 4). The message carries the Java class and message.
errors.Internal: An unexpected error inside the client. Please report it with the message.
errors.Cancelled: The user dismissed a form or picker.
errors.NotSupported: The op cannot run in this context (e.g. an interactive prompt on a headless session).
errors.GobGone: The game object no longer exists (out of view, destroyed, or picked up).
errors.ItemGone: The item widget no longer exists (moved, used up, or its container closed).
errors.UnknownOp: No op with that name exists in this client version.
errors.NoSuchArea: No area with that id, name or specialisation exists.
errors.PathNotFound: The pathfinder found no route to the target.
errors.AuthFailed: The handshake token was wrong or missing.
errors.WidgetGone: The window or widget no longer exists.
errors.NotFound: Something the op needed (a window, a menu option, an item) was not found.
